92 // TODO: This code is identical to 'FortranCodeGeneration_locatedNode::curprint'. Factor this!
93 void
94 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::curprint (const std::string & str) const
95 {
96 #if USE_RICE_FORTRAN_WRAPPING
97 
98  if( unp->currentFile != NULL && unp->currentFile->get_Fortran_only() )
99  {
100  // determine line wrapping parameters -- 'pos' variables are one-based
101  bool is_fixed_format = unp->currentFile->get_outputFormat() == SgFile::e_fixed_form_output_format;
102  bool is_free_format = unp->currentFile->get_outputFormat() == SgFile::e_free_form_output_format;
103  int usable_cols = ( is_fixed_format ? MAX_F90_LINE_LEN_FIXED
104  : is_free_format ? MAX_F90_LINE_LEN_FREE - 1 // reserve a column in free-format for possible trailing '&'
105  : unp->cur.get_linewrap() );
106 
107  // check whether line wrapping is needed
108  int used_cols = unp->cur.current_col(); // 'current_col' is zero-based
109  int free_cols = usable_cols - used_cols;
110  if( str.size() > free_cols )
111  {
112  if( is_fixed_format )
113  {
114  // only noncomment lines need wrapping
115  if( ! (used_cols == 0 && str[0] != ' ' ) )
116  {
117  // warn if successful wrapping is impossible
118  if( 6 + str.size() > usable_cols )
119  printf("Warning: can't wrap long line in Fortran fixed format (continuation + text is longer than a line)\n");
120 
121  // emit fixed-format line continuation
122  unp->cur.insert_newline(1);
123  unp->u_sage->curprint(" &");
124  }
125  }
126  else if( is_free_format )
127  {
128  // warn if successful wrapping is impossible
129  if( str.size() > usable_cols )
130  printf("Warning: can't wrap long line in Fortran free format (text is longer than a line)\n");
131 
132  // emit free-format line continuation even if result will still be too long
133  unp->u_sage->curprint("&");
134  unp->cur.insert_newline(1);
135  unp->u_sage->curprint("&");
136  }
137  else
138  printf("Warning: long line not wrapped (unknown output format)\n");
139  }
140  }
141 
142  unp->u_sage->curprint(str);
143 
144 #else // ! USE_RICE_FORTRAN_WRAPPING
145 
146  // FMZ (3/22/2010) added fortran continue line support
147  bool is_fortran90 = (unp->currentFile != NULL ) &&
148  (unp->currentFile->get_F90_only() ||
149  unp->currentFile->get_CoArrayFortran_only());
150 
151  int str_len = str.size();
152  int curr_line_len = unp->cur.current_col();
153 
154  if (is_fortran90 &&
155  curr_line_len!=0 &&
156  (str_len + curr_line_len)> MAX_F90_LINE_LEN) {
157  unp->u_sage->curprint("&");
158  unp->cur.insert_newline(1);
159  }
160 
161  if (is_fortran90)
162  {
163  if (str_len <= MAX_F90_LINE_LEN || str[0] == '#' || str[0] == '!')
164  {
165  unp->u_sage->curprint(str);
166  }
167  else
168  {
169  for (int stridx=0; stridx <str_len; stridx += MAX_F90_LINE_LEN)
170  {
171  std::string substring = str.substr(stridx, std::min(MAX_F90_LINE_LEN,str_len-stridx));
172  unp->u_sage->curprint(substring);
173  if (stridx + MAX_F90_LINE_LEN < str_len)
174  {
175  unp->u_sage->curprint("&");
176  unp->cur.insert_newline(1);
177  }
178  }
179  }
180  }
181  else
182  {
183  unp->u_sage->curprint(str);
184  }
185 
186 #endif // USE_RICE_FORTRAN_WRAPPING
187 }

1015 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseLineDirectives ( SgStatement* stmt )
1016  {
1017  // DQ (12/4/2007): This is the control for the output of #line "" directives
1018  if (unp->opt.get_linefile_opt() == true)
1019  {
1020  static int previousFileId = 0;
1021  static int previousLineNumber = 0;
1022  int currentFileId = stmt->get_startOfConstruct()->get_file_id();
1023  int currentLineNumber = stmt->get_startOfConstruct()->get_line();
1024  bool outputdirective = true;
1025 
1026  // There are a number of IR nodes that we don't want to have generate #line directives.
1027  if ( (isSgGlobal(stmt) != nullptr) ||
1028  (isSgFunctionDefinition(stmt) != nullptr) ||
1029  (isSgClassDefinition(stmt) != nullptr) ||
1030  (isSgBasicBlock(stmt) != nullptr) )
1031  {
1032  outputdirective = false;
1033  }
1034 
1035  if (outputdirective == true && ( (currentFileId == previousFileId) && (currentLineNumber == previousLineNumber) ))
1036  {
1037  outputdirective = false;
1038  }
1039  else
1040  {
1041  previousFileId = currentFileId;
1042  previousLineNumber = currentLineNumber;

1059 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::canBeUnparsedFromTokenStream(SgSourceFile* sourceFile, SgStatement* stmt)
1060  {
1061  // This function factors out the details of the conditions under which a statement can be unparsed from the token stream.
1062  // Note that it is conditional upon if there is a mapping identified between the token stream and the statement. These
1063  // mapping can be shared across more than one statement, or not exist, depending on the statement and the use of macro
1064  // expansion in the statement (or across multiple statements).
1065 
1066  // Note that we might want this function to return a pointer to a TokenStreamSequenceToNodeMapping instead (and NULL if no info is available)
1067 
1068  ASSERT_not_null(sourceFile);
1069  ASSERT_not_null(stmt);
1070 
1071 #define DEBUG_CAN_BE_UNPARSED 0
1072 
1073  bool canBeUnparsed = false;
1074 
1075 #if 0
1076  printf ("In canBeUnparsedFromTokenStream(): sourceFile = %p = %s filename = %s \n",sourceFile,sourceFile->class_name().c_str(),sourceFile->getFileName().c_str());
1077  printf (" --- stmt = %p = %s \n",stmt,stmt->class_name().c_str());
1078 #endif
1079 
1080 #if 0
1081  if (Rose::tokenSubsequenceMapOfMapsBySourceFile.find(sourceFile) != Rose::tokenSubsequenceMapOfMapsBySourceFile.end())
1082  {
1083  printf ("sourceFile = %p IS in Rose::tokenSubsequenceMapOfMapsBySourceFile \n",sourceFile);
1084  }
1085  else
1086  {
1087  printf ("sourceFile = %p is NOT in Rose::tokenSubsequenceMapOfMapsBySourceFile \n",sourceFile);
1088  }
1089 #endif
1090 
1091  std::map<SgNode*,TokenStreamSequenceToNodeMapping*> & tokenStreamSequenceMap = sourceFile->get_tokenSubsequenceMap();
1092 
1093  // If a set of statements are associated with the same interval of the token stream, then we have to detect this.
1094  // The first statement will be mapped to the token stream, but then I am less clear on what happens.
1095 
1096  if (tokenStreamSequenceMap.find(stmt) != tokenStreamSequenceMap.end())
1097  {
1098  TokenStreamSequenceToNodeMapping* tokenSubsequence = tokenStreamSequenceMap[stmt];
1099  // ASSERT_not_null(tokenSubsequence);
1100  if (tokenSubsequence != NULL)
1101  {
1102 #if DEBUG_CAN_BE_UNPARSED
1103  printf ("In canBeUnparsedFromTokenStream(): stmt = %p = %s \n",stmt,stmt->class_name().c_str());
1104  printf (" --- tokenStreamSequenceMap: leading (start,end) = (%d,%d) \n",tokenSubsequence->leading_whitespace_start, tokenSubsequence->leading_whitespace_end);
1105  printf (" --- tokenStreamSequenceMap: node (start,end) = (%d,%d) \n",tokenSubsequence->token_subsequence_start, tokenSubsequence->token_subsequence_end);
1106  printf (" --- tokenStreamSequenceMap: trailing (start,end) = (%d,%d) \n",tokenSubsequence->trailing_whitespace_start,tokenSubsequence->trailing_whitespace_end);
1107 #endif
1108  ASSERT_not_null(stmt->get_file_info());
1109 
1110 #if DEBUG_CAN_BE_UNPARSED
1111  stmt->get_file_info()->display("In canBeUnparsedFromTokenStream(): debug");
1112 #endif
1113  canBeUnparsed = (tokenSubsequence->token_subsequence_start != -1);
1114 
1115  // DQ (11/29/2013): Added support for the detection of redundantly mapped statements to token sequences.
1116  // E.g. ROSE normalizations of variable declaration with multiple variables into seperate (multiple)
1117  // SgVariableDeclaration IR nodes in the AST.
1118  std::multimap<int,SgStatement*> & redundantlyMappedTokensToStatementMultimap = sourceFile->get_redundantlyMappedTokensToStatementMultimap();
1119 
1120  std::set<int> & redundantTokenEndings = sourceFile->get_redundantTokenEndingsSet();
1121 
1122  std::set<int>::iterator k = redundantTokenEndings.begin();
1123  while (k != redundantTokenEndings.end())
1124  {
1125  int lastTokenIndex = *k;
1126 
1127 #if DEBUG_CAN_BE_UNPARSED
1128  printf ("Redundant statement list: lastTokenIndex = %d \n",lastTokenIndex);
1129 #endif
1130  std::pair<std::multimap<int,SgStatement*>::iterator,std::multimap<int,SgStatement*>::iterator> range_iterator = redundantlyMappedTokensToStatementMultimap.equal_range(lastTokenIndex);
1131  std::multimap<int,SgStatement*>::iterator first_iterator = range_iterator.first;
1132  std::multimap<int,SgStatement*>::iterator last_iterator = range_iterator.second;
1133 
1134  std::multimap<int,SgStatement*>::iterator local_iterator = first_iterator;
1135  while (local_iterator != last_iterator)
1136  {
1137 
1138 #if DEBUG_CAN_BE_UNPARSED
1139  SgStatement* stmt = local_iterator->second;
1140  printf (" --- redundant statement for lastTokenIndex = %d stmt = %p = %s \n",lastTokenIndex,stmt,stmt->class_name().c_str());
1141 #endif
1142  local_iterator++;
1143  }
1144 
1145  k++;
1146  }
1147  }
1148  }
1149  else
1150  {
1151 
1152 #if DEBUG_CAN_BE_UNPARSED || 0
1153  printf ("Note: In canBeUnparsedFromTokenStream(): the requested subsequence mapping object was not found: stmt = %p = %s \n",stmt,stmt->class_name().c_str());
1154 #endif
1155  }
1156 
1157 #if DEBUG_CAN_BE_UNPARSED || 0

1159 #endif

1161  // DQ (9/3/2021): Debugging code for test in the roseTests/astTokenStreamTests.
1162  // I think that the artifical frontiers are not being marked properly, or we are using a different mechanism

1174  printf ("Exiting as a test! \n");
1175  ROSE_ASSERT(false);
1176 #endif
1177  }
1178 
1179  return canBeUnparsed;
1180  }

3716  // We need to evaluate how the last statement in the SgBasicBlock (and any scope) so that we can output the trailing whitespace generally.
3717  // This shoud not be handled in the unparse function for the SgBasicBlock since that would be more complex.
3718 
3719  // There are three approaches:
3720  // 1) We could iterate over the statements in the scope and find the last statement that would be unparsed, then that is the last statement.
3721  // 2) We can't just look at the last statement in the scope directly, since it might not have been unparsed in this file.
3722  // 3) Better might be to iterate backwards over the statements in the scope to find the first statement that would be unparsed, and then
3723  // that is the last statement. I like this last idea the best.
3724

3734  if (scopeStatement->containsOnlyDeclarations() == true)

3741  while (foundStatementToUnparse == false && i != declarationStatementPtrList.rend())

3753  }

4691 // will not print out file information
4692 //-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4693 void
4694 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseExpression(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info & info)
4695  {
4696  ASSERT_not_null(expr);
4697  ASSERT_require(info.SkipClassDefinition() == info.SkipEnumDefinition());
4698  ASSERT_not_null(expr->get_startOfConstruct());
4699  ASSERT_not_null(expr->get_file_info());
4700 
4701  // Fails when merging ASTs loaded from files
4702  bool ROSE_2423__bypass = ( expr->get_file_info() == expr->get_operatorPosition() );
4703  ROSE_ASSERT(expr->get_file_info()->isCompilerGenerated() == expr->get_startOfConstruct()->isCompilerGenerated() || ROSE_2423__bypass);
4704 
4705  // Ignore the case of a transformation
4706  if (expr->get_endOfConstruct() == nullptr && expr->get_file_info()->isTransformation() == false)
4707  {
4708  printf ("Error in unparseExpression(): expr = %p = %s expr->get_endOfConstruct() == NULL \n",expr,expr->class_name().c_str());
4709  expr->get_file_info()->display("unparseExpression (debug)");
4710  }
4711 
4712  if ( unparseLineReplacement(expr,info) )
4713  {
4714  return;
4715  }
4716 
4717  // Unparse directives before the current expression
4718  unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(expr, info, PreprocessingInfo::before);
4719 
4720  SgExpression* expressionTree = nullptr;
4721  switch (expr->variantT()) {
4722  case V_SgVarRefExp:
4723  {
4724  expressionTree = isSgExpression(isSgVarRefExp(expr)->get_originalExpressionTree());
4725  break;
4726  }
4727  case V_SgCastExp:
4728  {
4729  expressionTree = isSgExpression(isSgCastExp(expr)->get_originalExpressionTree());
4730  break;
4731  }
4732  default:
4733  {
4734  SgFunctionRefExp * func_ref = isSgFunctionRefExp(expr);
4735  if (func_ref) {
4736  expressionTree = isSgExpression(func_ref->get_originalExpressionTree());
4737  }
4738  }
4739  }
4740 
4741  AstUnparseAttribute* unparseAttribute = dynamic_cast<AstUnparseAttribute*>(expr->getAttribute(AstUnparseAttribute::markerName));
4742  if (unparseAttribute != nullptr)
4743  {
4744  string code = unparseAttribute->toString(AstUnparseAttribute::e_before);
4745  curprint (code);
4746  }
4747 
4748  // Only replace the unparsing of the IR node with a string if a string is marked as AstUnparseAttribute::e_replace.
4749  if (unparseAttribute != nullptr && unparseAttribute->replacementStringExists() == true)
4750  {
4751  string code = unparseAttribute->toString(AstUnparseAttribute::e_replace);
4752  curprint (code);
4753  }
4754  else if (expressionTree != nullptr && info.SkipConstantFoldedExpressions() == false)
4755  {
4756  unparseExpression(expressionTree, info);
4757  }
4758  else
4759  {
4760  bool printParen = requiresParentheses(expr,info);
4761 
4762  if (printParen)
4763  {
4764  if (isSgMatrixExp(expr))
4765  {
4766  printParen = false;
4767  }
4768  else
4769  {
4770  // Make sure this is not an expression list
4771  ASSERT_require(isSgExprListExp(expr) == nullptr);
4772  // Output the left paren
4773  curprint ("(");
4774  }
4775  }
4776 
4777  switch (expr->variant())
4778  {
4779  case UNARY_EXPRESSION:
4780  {
4781  printf ("This should never be called: case UNARY_EXPRESSION\n");
4782  ROSE_ABORT();
4783 
4784  unparseUnaryExpr (expr, info);
4785  break;
4786  }
4787 
4788  case BINARY_EXPRESSION:
4789  {
4790  printf ("This should never be called: case BINARY_EXPRESSION\n");
4791  ROSE_ABORT();
4792 
4793  unparseBinaryExpr(expr, info);
4794  break;
4795  }
4796 
4797  case MATRIX_EXP:
4798  {
4799  unparseMatrixExp(expr, info);
4800  break;
4801  }
4802 
4803  case EXPR_LIST: { unparseExprList(expr, info); break; }
4804 
4805  case NULLPTR_VAL:
4806 
4807  // These cases are separated out so that we can handle the original expression tree
4808  // from any possible constant folding by EDG.
4809  case BOOL_VAL:
4810  case SHORT_VAL:
4811  case CHAR_VAL:
4812  case SIGNED_CHAR_VAL:
4813  case UNSIGNED_CHAR_VAL:
4814  case WCHAR_VAL:
4815  case STRING_VAL:
4816  case UNSIGNED_SHORT_VAL:
4817  case ENUM_VAL:
4818  case INT_VAL:
4819  case UNSIGNED_INT_VAL:
4820  case LONG_INT_VAL:
4821  case LONG_LONG_INT_VAL:
4822  case UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG_INT_VAL:
4823  case UNSIGNED_LONG_INT_VAL:
4824  case FLOAT_VAL:
4825  case DOUBLE_VAL:
4826  case LONG_DOUBLE_VAL:
4827  case COMPLEX_VAL:
4828  {
4829  unparseValue(expr, info);
4830  break;
4831  }
4832 
4833  default:
4834  {
4835  // Call the derived class implementation for language specific unparsing.
4836  unparseLanguageSpecificExpression(expr,info);
4837  break;
4838  }
4839  }
4840 
4841  if (printParen)
4842  {
4843  // Output the right paren
4844  curprint (")");
4845  }
4846 
4847  } // unparse source replacement END
4848 
4849 #if OUTPUT_EMBEDDED_COLOR_CODES_FOR_EXPRESSIONS
4850  if (get_embedColorCodesInGeneratedCode() > 0)
4851  {
4852  printColorCodes ( expr, false, stateVector );
4853  }
4854 #endif
4855 
4856  // DQ (7/20/2008): Part of new support for unparsing arbitrary strings into the unparsed code.
4857  if (unparseAttribute != NULL)
4858  {
4859  string code = unparseAttribute->toString(AstUnparseAttribute::e_after);
4860  curprint (code);
4861  }
4862 
4863  // DQ (7/19/2008): This is the new code to unparse directives before the current expression
4864  unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(expr, info, PreprocessingInfo::after);
4865 
4866 #if OUTPUT_DEBUGGING_FUNCTION_BOUNDARIES || 0
4867  // DQ (8/21/2005): Suppress comments when unparsing to build type names
4868  if ( !info.SkipComments() || !info.SkipCPPDirectives() )
4869  {
4870  printf ("Leaving unparse expression (%p): sage_class_name() = %s \n",expr,expr->sage_class_name());
4871  curprint ( "\n/* Bottom of unparseExpression " + expr->class_name() + " */ \n");
4872  }
4873 #endif
4874 
4875  // DQ (9/9/2016): These should have been setup to be the same.
4876  ROSE_ASSERT(info.SkipClassDefinition() == info.SkipEnumDefinition());
4877  }

5251 #endif
5252  }

5269  // DQ (5/27/2005): Added support for compiler-generated statements that might appear at the end of the applications
5270  // printf ("At end of unparseGlobalStmt \n");
5271  // outputCompilerGeneratedStatements(info);

5273 #if DEBUG_USING_CURPRINT
5274  curprint(string("\n/* Leaving unparseGlobalStmt(): global scope size = ") + StringUtility::numberToString(globalScope->get_declarations().size()) + " */ \n");

5276 
5277 #if 0
5278  printf ("Leaving UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseGlobalStmt() \n\n");

5280 
5281 #if 0
5282  printf ("Exiting as a test! \n");
5283  ROSE_ABORT();

5286  // DQ (12/10/2014): Moved to the locate in the false block of if (sourceFile->get_unparse_tokens() == true).

5326 bool
5327 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseLineReplacement( SgLocatedNode* stmt, SgUnparse_Info& info )
5328  {
5329  int replacedLines = 0;
5330 
5331  // Get atached preprocessing info
5332  AttachedPreprocessingInfoType* prepInfoPtr = stmt->getAttachedPreprocessingInfo();
5333  if (prepInfoPtr == nullptr)
5334  {
5335  // There's no preprocessing info attached to the current statement
5336  return false;
5337  }
5338 
5339  // If we are skipping BOTH comments and CPP directives then there is nothing to do
5340  if ( info.SkipComments() && info.SkipCPPDirectives() )
5341  {
5342  return false;
5343  }
5344 
5345  // Traverse the container of PreprocessingInfo objects
5346  AttachedPreprocessingInfoType::iterator i;
5347  for (i = prepInfoPtr->begin(); i != prepInfoPtr->end(); ++i)
5348  {
5349  // i is a pointer to the current prepInfo object, print current preprocessing info
5350  ASSERT_not_null( (*i));
5351  ROSE_ASSERT ( (*i)->getTypeOfDirective() != PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration );
5352  ROSE_ASSERT ( (*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::before ||
5353  (*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::end_of ||
5354  (*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::after ||
5355  (*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::inside );
5356 
5357  // Check and see if the info object would indicate that the statement would
5358  // be printed, if not then don't print the comments associated with it.
5359  // These might have to be handled on a case by case basis.
5360  bool infoSaysGoAhead = !info.SkipEnumDefinition() && !info.SkipClassDefinition() && !info.SkipFunctionDefinition();
5361 
5362  // Allow expressions to have their associated comments unparsed.
5363  infoSaysGoAhead = (infoSaysGoAhead == true) || (isSgExpression(stmt) != nullptr);
5364 
5365  switch ( (*i)->getTypeOfDirective() )
5366  {
5367  case PreprocessingInfo::LineReplacement:
5368  {
5369  if (isSgExpression(stmt) == nullptr) {
5370  // Do this when line replacement matches a whole statement
5371  unp->cur.format(stmt, info, FORMAT_BEFORE_DIRECTIVE);
5372  }
5373  curprint( (*i)->getString() );
5374 
5375  replacedLines++;
5376  break;
5377  }
5378  default:
5379  break;
5380  }
5381  }
5382 
5383  // there should only be one line replacement directive for a statement
5384  ASSERT_require(replacedLines <= 1);
5385 
5386  return (replacedLines > 0);
5387  }

5389 void
5390 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(
5391  SgLocatedNode* stmt,
5392  SgUnparse_Info& info,
5393  PreprocessingInfo::RelativePositionType whereToUnparse)
5394  {
5395  // Get atached preprocessing info
5396  AttachedPreprocessingInfoType *prepInfoPtr = stmt->getAttachedPreprocessingInfo();
5397 
5398  if (prepInfoPtr == nullptr)
5399  {
5400  // There's no preprocessing info attached to the current statement
5401  return;
5402  }
5403 
5404  // If we are skiping BOTH comments and CPP directives then there is nothing to do
5405  if ( info.SkipComments() && info.SkipCPPDirectives() )
5406  {
5407  // There's no preprocessing info attached to the current statement
5408  return;
5409  }
5410 
5411  // Traverse the container of PreprocessingInfo objects
5412  AttachedPreprocessingInfoType::iterator i;
5413  for (i = prepInfoPtr->begin(); i != prepInfoPtr->end(); ++i)
5414  {
5415  // i is a pointer to the current prepInfo object, print current preprocessing info
5416  ASSERT_not_null((*i));
5417  ROSE_ASSERT ((*i)->getTypeOfDirective() != PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration);
5418  ROSE_ASSERT ((*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::before ||
5419  (*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::end_of ||
5420  (*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::after ||
5421  (*i)->getRelativePosition() == PreprocessingInfo::inside);
5422 
5423  // Check and see if the info object would indicate that the statement would
5424  // be printed, if not then don't print the comments associated with it.
5425  // These might have to be handled on a case by case basis.
5426  bool infoSaysGoAhead = !info.SkipEnumDefinition() &&
5427  !info.SkipClassDefinition() &&
5428  !info.SkipFunctionDefinition();
5429 
5430  // Allow expressions to have there associated comments unparsed.
5431  infoSaysGoAhead = (infoSaysGoAhead == true) || (isSgExpression(stmt) != nullptr) || (isSgInitializedName (stmt) != nullptr) || (isSgHeaderFileBody(stmt) != nullptr);
5432 
5433  ASSERT_not_null(*i);
5434  bool isCommentFromCurrentFile = true;
5435  bool isSharedLocatedNode = (stmt->get_file_info()->isShared() == true);
5436 
5437  // DQ (3/12/2019): Only review the decission to reset infoSaysGoAhead if it is true.
5438  if (isSharedLocatedNode == true && infoSaysGoAhead == true && info.get_current_source_file() != NULL)
5439  {
5440  ASSERT_not_null(info.get_current_source_file()->get_file_info());
5441 
5442  // DQ (2/27/2019): If this is a comment from a different file (not current file) then we can't unparse it here.
5443  isCommentFromCurrentFile = (info.get_current_source_file()->get_file_info()->get_file_id() == (*i)->getFileId());
5444 
5445  if (isCommentFromCurrentFile == false)
5446  {
5447  // DQ (3/2/2019): I will alow this for now, but it is an inappropriate use of the Sg_File_Info object to define a file that does not exist.
5448  if ( ((*i)->get_file_info()->get_filenameString() == "Compiler-Generated in PRE") ||
5449  ((*i)->get_file_info()->get_filenameString() =="Compiler-Generated in Finite Differencing") ||
5450  ((*i)->get_file_info()->isTransformation() == true) )
5451  {
5452  // Don't suppress the output of ROSE generated comments in this case.
5453  }
5454  else
5455  {
5456  infoSaysGoAhead = false;
5457  }
5458  }
5459  }
5460 
5461  // DQ (2/5/2003):
5462  // The old directive handling allows all the test codes to parse properly, but
5463  // is not sufficent for handling the A++ transformations which are more complex.
5464  // I am trying to recover the old way which permitted all the test codes to work
5465  // before I fix it to be consistant with how it must work for the A++ transformation
5466  // to work properly. This is work that was unfinished by Markus K. summer 2002.
5467  // (Though he did do a great job not enough information was provided in SAGE from EDG
5468  // to finish it (I think)).
5469 
5470  // DQ (2/18/2003): Work to allow all CPP directives to be unparsed correctly on a statement
5471  // by statement basis has been completed, tested, and checked in.
5472 
5473  if (infoSaysGoAhead && (*i)->getRelativePosition() == whereToUnparse)
5474  {
5475  unp->cur.format(stmt, info, FORMAT_BEFORE_DIRECTIVE);
5476 
5477  if (unp->opt.get_unparse_includes_opt() == true)
5478  {
5479  // DQ (9/16/2013): This is an error for C style comments spanning more than one line.
5480  // To fix this just unparse the comment directly, since the syntax to make it a comment
5481  // is included in the string.
5482  // Original comment: If we are unparsing the include files then we can simplify the
5483  // CPP directive processing and unparse them all as comments!
5484  // Comments can also be unparsed as comments (I think!).
5485  // curprint ( "// " + (*i)->getString());
5486 
5487  switch ( (*i)->getTypeOfDirective() )
5488  {
5489  // Comments don't have to be further commented
5490  case PreprocessingInfo::FortranStyleComment:
5491  case PreprocessingInfo::F90StyleComment:
5492  case PreprocessingInfo::C_StyleComment:
5493  case PreprocessingInfo::CplusplusStyleComment:
5494  if ( !info.SkipComments() )
5495  {
5496  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5497  }
5498  break;
5499 
5500  default:
5501  {
5502  if ((*i)->getNumberOfLines() == 1)
5503  {
5504  // DQ (9/16/2013): Commented out single line CPP directives is easy, so go ahead and do that.
5505  // This used later style C comment syntax. This permits the user to see the original CPP
5506  // directives in a way that they will have no effect.
5507  curprint("// " + (*i)->getString());
5508  }
5509  else
5510  {
5511  // DQ (9/16/2013): Multi-line CPP directives are a bit more complex so ignore them.
5512  curprint("/* multi-line CPP directive ignored (no robust way to comment them out yet implemented) */\n");
5513  }
5514  }
5515  }
5516  }
5517  else
5518  {
5519  // DQ (1/28/2013): Fixed indentation of code block.
5520  switch ( (*i)->getTypeOfDirective() )
5521  {
5522  // All #include directives are unparsed so that we can make the
5523  // output codes as similar as possible to the input codes. This also
5524  // simplifies the debugging. On the down side it sets up a chain of
5525  // problems that force us to unparse most of the other directives
5526  // which makes the unparsing a bit more complex.
5527  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIncludeDeclaration:
5528  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIncludeNextDeclaration:
5529  if ( !info.SkipComments() )
5530  {
5531  ROSE_ASSERT(unp->opt.get_unparse_includes_opt() == false);
5532 #if 1
5533  // DQ (9/16/2013): This is simpler code.
5534  curprint((*i)->getString());
5535 #else
5536  // DQ (9/16/2013): This predicate should be always false.
5537  if (unp->opt.get_unparse_includes_opt() == true)
5538  curprint ( string("// " ) + (*i)->getString());
5539  else
5540  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5541 #endif
5542  }
5543  break;
5544 
5545  // Comments don't have to be further commented
5546  case PreprocessingInfo::AdaStyleComment:
5547  case PreprocessingInfo::FortranStyleComment:
5548  case PreprocessingInfo::F90StyleComment:
5549  case PreprocessingInfo::JovialStyleComment:
5550  case PreprocessingInfo::C_StyleComment:
5551  case PreprocessingInfo::CplusplusStyleComment:
5552  if ( !info.SkipComments() )
5553  {
5554  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5555  }
5556  break;
5557 
5558  // extern declarations must be handled as comments since the EDG frontend strips them away
5559  case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationStart:
5560  case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationEnd:
5561  if ( !info.SkipComments() )
5562  {
5563 #if 0
5564  curprint ( string("/* case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecification (Start/End)") + (*i)->getString() + " */ \n");
5565 #endif
5566  if (unp->opt.get_unparse_includes_opt() == true)
5567  curprint ( string("// ") + (*i)->getString());
5568  else
5569  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5570 #if 0
5571  curprint ( string("/* DONE: case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecification (Start/End)") + (*i)->getString() + " */ \n");
5572 #endif
5573 
5574  if ( (*i)->getTypeOfDirective() == PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationStart)
5575  {
5576 #if 0
5577  printf ("calling info.set_extern_C_with_braces(true) \n");
5578 #endif
5579 #if 0
5580  curprint ( string("/* calling info.set_extern_C_with_braces(true): case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationStart") + (*i)->getString() + " */ \n");
5581 #endif
5582  info.set_extern_C_with_braces(true);
5583  }
5584  else
5585  {
5586  ROSE_ASSERT( (*i)->getTypeOfDirective() == PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationEnd );
5587 #if 0
5588  printf ("calling info.set_extern_C_with_braces(false) \n");
5589 #endif
5590 #if 0
5591  curprint ( string("/* calling info.set_extern_C_with_braces(true): case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationEnd") + (*i)->getString() + " */ \n");
5592 #endif
5593  info.set_extern_C_with_braces(false);
5594  }
5595 
5596  }
5597  break;
5598 
5599  // Must unparse these because they could hide a #define
5600  // directive which would then be seen e.g.
5601  // #if 0
5602  // #define printf parallelPrintf
5603  // #endif
5604  // So because we unparse the #define we must unparse
5605  // the #if, #ifdef, #else, and #endif directives.
5606  // line declarations should also appear in the output
5607  // to permit the debugger to see the original code
5608  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIfdefDeclaration:
5609  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIfndefDeclaration:
5610  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIfDeclaration:
5611  // Rama (08/17/07): Adding support so that pseudo-comments can be attached properly.
5612  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorDeadIfDeclaration:
5613  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorElseDeclaration:
5614  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorElifDeclaration:
5615  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorEndifDeclaration:
5616  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorEnd_ifDeclaration: // Ada "end if"
5617  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorElsifDeclaration: // Ada "elsif"
5618  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorLineDeclaration:
5619  // AS(120506) Added support for skipped tokens for Wave
5620  case PreprocessingInfo::CSkippedToken:
5621  if ( !info.SkipComments() )
5622  {
5623  if (unp->opt.get_unparse_includes_opt() == true)
5624  {
5625  curprint ( string("// (previously processed: ignored) " ) + (*i)->getString());
5626  }
5627  else
5628  {
5629  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5630  }
5631  }
5632  else
5633  {
5634  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5635  }
5636  break;
5637 
5638  // Comment out these declarations where they occur because we don't need
5639  // them (they have already been evaluated by the front-end and would be
5640  // redundent).
5641  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorWarningDeclaration:
5642  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorErrorDeclaration:
5643  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorEmptyDeclaration:
5644  if ( !info.SkipCPPDirectives() )
5645  {
5646  // DQ (11/29/2006): Let's try to generate code which handles these better.
5647  // curprint ( string("// (previously processed: ignored) " + (*i)->getString() ;
5648  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5649  }
5650  break;
5651 
5652  // We skip commenting out these cases for the moment
5653  // We must unparse these since they could control the path
5654  // taken in header files included separately e.g.
5655  // #define OPTIMIZE_ME
5656  // // optimization.h could include two paths dependent on the value of OPTIMIZE_ME
5657  // #include "optimization.h"
5658  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorDefineDeclaration:
5659  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUndefDeclaration:
5660  if ( !info.SkipCPPDirectives() )
5661  {
5662  if (unp->opt.get_unparse_includes_opt() == true)
5663  {
5664  curprint(string("// (previously processed: ignored) " ) + (*i)->getString());
5665  }
5666  else
5667  {
5668  // curprint((*i)->getString());
5669 
5670  // DQ (12/30/2013): Handle the case of a self referential macro declaration e.g. "#define foo X->foo".
5671  if ((*i)->getTypeOfDirective() == PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorDefineDeclaration)
5672  {
5673 #if 0
5674  printf ("In unparser: CPP macro = %s \n",(*i)->getString().c_str());
5675 #endif
5676  // We need to supress the output of self-referential macros since they will be expanded
5677  // twice in the back-end compilation of the ROSE generated code.
5678  bool isSelfReferential = (*i)->isSelfReferential();
5679 #if 0
5680  printf ("In unparser: isSelfReferential = %s CPP macro = %s \n",isSelfReferential ? "true" : "false",(*i)->getString().c_str());
5681 #endif
5682  if (isSelfReferential == true)
5683  {
5684 #if 0
5685  // DQ (12/31/2013): Note that the final CR is a part of the CPP #define directive (so we don't need another one).
5686  printf ("Detected self-referential macro (supressed in generated code) macro = %s ",(*i)->getString().c_str());
5687 #endif
5688  // DQ (12/31/2013): We can't use /* */ to comment out the #define macro since it might also include a "/* ... */" substring.
5689  // curprint(string("/* (previously processed: ignoring self-referential macro declaration) " ) + (*i)->getString() + " */\n");
5690  // curprint(string("// (previously processed: ignoring self-referential macro declaration) " ) + (*i)->getString() + " \n");
5691 #if 0
5692  if ((*i)->getNumberOfLines() == 1)
5693  {
5694  // DQ (1/21/2014): This reports: "error: stray '#' in program"
5695  // curprint(string("// (previously processed: ignoring self-referential macro declaration) " ) + (*i)->getString() + " \n");
5696  curprint(string("// (previously processed: ignoring self-referential macro declaration) " ) + (*i)->getMacroName() + " \n");
5697  }
5698  else
5699  {
5700  ROSE_ASSERT((*i)->getNumberOfLines() > 1);
5701  curprint(string("/* (previously processed: ignoring self-referential macro declaration) " ) + (*i)->getMacroName() + " */\n");
5702  }
5703 #else
5704  // DQ (1/21/2014): This has to be a C style comments for the options used in Valgrind compilation (not C99, I think).
5705  curprint(string("/* (previously processed: ignoring self-referential macro declaration) macro name = " ) + (*i)->getMacroName() + " */ \n");
5706 #endif
5707  }
5708  else
5709  {
5710  curprint((*i)->getString());
5711  }
5712  }
5713  else
5714  {
5715  curprint((*i)->getString());
5716  }
5717  }
5718  }
5719  break;
5720 
5721  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration:
5722  printf ("Error: CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration found \n");
5723  ROSE_ABORT();
5724  break;
5725  case PreprocessingInfo::CMacroCall:
5726  // AS(1/04/07) Macro rewrapping is currently not supported
5727  break;
5728  case PreprocessingInfo::CMacroCallStatement:
5729  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5730  break;
5731 
5732  case PreprocessingInfo::LineReplacement:
5733  break;
5734 
5735  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIdentDeclaration:
5736  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5737  break;
5738 
5739  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorCompilerGeneratedLinemarker:
5740  curprint ( (*i)->getString());
5741  break;
5742 
5743  default:
5744  printf ("Error: default reached in switch in Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo()\n");
5745  ROSE_ABORT();
5746  }
5747  }
5748 
5749  unp->cur.format(stmt, info, FORMAT_AFTER_DIRECTIVE);
5750  }
5751  }
5752 
5753 #if 0
5754  printf ("Leaving unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(): stmt = %p = %s \n",stmt,stmt->class_name().c_str());
5755  // curprint ("\n /* Inside of unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo() */ \n");
5756  curprint (string("/* Leaving unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo() stmt = ") + stmt->class_name() + " */ \n");
5757 #endif

5762 void
5763 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseUnaryExpr(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
5764  {
5765  SgUnaryOp* unary_op = isSgUnaryOp(expr);
5766  ASSERT_not_null(unary_op);
5767 
5768  info.set_nested_expression();
5769 
5770  //
5771  // Flag to indicate whether the operand contains an overloaded arrow operator
5772  //
5773  bool arrow_op = false;
5774  arrow_op = unp->u_sage->NoDereference(expr);
5775 
5776  // We have to test to see if the operand associated with this unary expression is a function pointer
5777  // then we can use either function pointer calling syntax
5778  // (for void (*functionPointer) (int) as a declaration):
5779  // 1) functionPointer (x);
5780  // 2) (*functionPointer) (x);
5781  // Either is valid syntax (see Stroustrup (2nd Edition) section 7.7 "Pointer to Function" page 156.)
5782  // It seems that EDG and SAGE represent the two similarly, so we have to choose which format we
5783  // want to have in the unparsing. Likely this should be an option to the unparser.
5784 
5785 
5786  // DQ (2/22/2005): Ignoring if this is a SgFunctionType (test ...)
5787  // Bugfix (2/26/2001) If this is for a function pointer then skip printing out
5788  // the operator name (for dereferencing operator)
5789  if (unary_op->get_mode() != SgUnaryOp::postfix)
5790  {
5791  // DQ (2/25/2005): Trap case of SgPointerDerefExp so that "*" can't be
5792  // turned into "/*" if preceeded by a SgDivideOp or overloaded "operator/()"
5793  // Put in an extra space so that if this happens we only generate "/ *"
5794  // test2005_09.C demonstrates this bug!
5795  if (isSgPointerDerefExp(expr) != NULL)
5796  {
5797  curprint(" ");
5798  }
5799  curprint(info.get_operator_name());
5800  }
5801 
5802  // DQ (1/25/2014): Added support to avoid unparsing "- -5" as "--5".
5803  SgValueExp* valueExp = isSgValueExp(unary_op->get_operand());
5804  SgMinusOp* minus_op = isSgMinusOp(unary_op);
5805  if (minus_op != NULL && valueExp != NULL)
5806  {
5807  // We need to make sure we don't unparse: "- -5" as "--5".
5808  // I think we need an isNegative() query function so that we could refine this test to only apply to negative literals.
5809  curprint(" ");
5810  }
5811 
5812  unparseExpression(unary_op->get_operand(), info);
5813 
5814  if (unary_op->get_mode() == SgUnaryOp::postfix && !arrow_op)
5815  {
5816  curprint(info.get_operator_name());

5823 bool
5824 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::isDotExprWithAnonymousUnion(SgExpression* expr)
5825  {
5826  // DQ (1/23/2014): This function support detecting when the supress the output of the SgDotExp
5827  // in the access of data members from un-named unions. Note that variables of type that are
5828  // un-named unions are given a unique generated name of the form "__anonymous_0x" as a
5829  // prefix to the pointer value of the declaration that defines the un-named union. The
5830  // handling here is not specific to unions and handles any type where the declaration is
5831  // using a generated name of this specific form.
5832 
5833  bool returnValue = false;
5834 
5835  SgDotExp* dotExp = isSgDotExp(expr);
5836  if (dotExp != NULL)
5837  {
5838  SgBinaryOp* binary_op = isSgBinaryOp(dotExp->get_lhs_operand());
5839  if (binary_op != NULL)
5840  {
5841  SgExpression* rhs = binary_op->get_rhs_operand();
5842  ASSERT_not_null(rhs);
5843  SgVarRefExp* varRefExp = isSgVarRefExp(rhs);
5844  if (varRefExp != NULL)
5845  {
5846  bool isAnonymousName = (string(varRefExp->get_symbol()->get_name()).substr(0,14) == "__anonymous_0x");
5847  returnValue = isAnonymousName;
5848  }
5849  }
5850  else
5851  {
5852  // The other case we have to handle is that the lhs is a SgVarRefExp to an un-named variable. See test2014_152.C.
5853  SgVarRefExp* varRefExp = isSgVarRefExp(dotExp->get_lhs_operand());
5854  if (varRefExp != NULL)
5855  {
5856  bool isAnonymousName = (string(varRefExp->get_symbol()->get_name()).substr(0,14) == "__anonymous_0x");
5857  returnValue = isAnonymousName;
5858  }
5859  }
5860  }
5861 
5862  return returnValue;
5863  }

6670  else
6671  {
6672 #if DEBUG_BINARY_OPERATORS
6673  printf ("++++++++++++++++ output of the RHS 3 (non-operator syntax used) \n");
6674  curprint ( "\n /* unparseBinaryExpr(): output RHS 3 */ \n");
6675 #endif
6676  ROSE_ASSERT(parent_function_call_uses_operator_syntax == false);
6677 
6678  unparseExpression(rhs, info);
6679 
6680 #if DEBUG_BINARY_OPERATORS
6681  curprint ( "\n /* DONE: unparseBinaryExpr(): output RHS 3 */ \n");
6682 #endif
6683  }
6684  }
6685 #if NEW_CASE
6686  else
6687  {
6688 #if DEBUG_BINARY_OPERATORS
6689  printf ("++++++++++++++++ skipping output of the RHS 4 \n");
6690 #endif
6691  // DQ (7/5/2014): Add assertions using simpler evaluation against stored valuses from the EDG translation.
6692  if (is_currently_a_function_call == true)
6693  {
6694  ROSE_ASSERT(current_function_call_uses_operator_syntax == true);
6695  ROSE_ASSERT(current_function_call_is_compiler_generated == true);
6696  }
6697  }
6698 #endif
6699 
6700 #if DEBUG_BINARY_OPERATORS
6701  curprint ( "\n /* unparseBinaryExpr(): Test 6 after unparseExpression() rhs = " + rhs->class_name() + "*/ \n");
6702 #endif
6703  }
6704 
6705  info.unset_nested_expression();
6706 
6707 #if DEBUG_BINARY_OPERATORS
6708  printf ("Leaving unparseBinaryExpr(): exp = %p = %s \n",expr,expr->class_name().c_str());
6709  curprint ( "\n /* Leaving unparseBinaryExpr (expr = " + expr->class_name() + " = " + StringUtility::numberToString(expr) + ") */ \n");
6710 #endif
6711  }

6715 bool
6716 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::isRequiredOperator(SgBinaryOp* binary_op, bool /*current_function_call_uses_operator_syntax*/, bool parent_function_call_uses_operator_syntax)
6717  {
6718  // DQ (4/14/2013): The mixing of overloaded operator names and operator syntax has been a bit complex.
6719  // There are special cases that are especially troubling, so this code tries to handle this.
6720  // ROSE now preserves the original form of the operator if it was used as either:
6721  // 1) the overloaded operator name, e.g. "i = result.operator&()->size();", or
6722  // 2) using the operator syntax, e,g, "i = (&result)->size();"
6723  // There are different function resolution lookup rules for each type of representaion.
6724  // So this is a subtle area of C++ to start with. ROSE tracks in the IR (in the SgFunctionCallExp)
6725  // if the function call uses the operator syntax (data member, p_uses_operator_syntax, with
6726  // set and get access functions automatically generated by ROSETTA.
6727 
6728  // Some complex examples are:
6729  // 1) "i = result.operator&()->size();" vs. "i = (&result)->size();", the use of SgArrowOp "->" is required.
6730  // 2) "ref.operator->()->getFormat();" vs. "ref->getFormat();", the use of SgArrowOp "->" is supressed.
6731  // 3) "s.operator&();" vs. "&s;", example of prefix operator syntax.
6732 
6733  bool returnValue = false;
6734  bool isArrowExp = (isSgArrowExp(binary_op) != nullptr);
6735  if (isArrowExp == true)
6736  {
6737  return true;
6738  }
6739 
6740  SgExpression* lhs = binary_op->get_lhs_operand();
6741  ASSERT_not_null(lhs);
6742 
6743  SgType* lhs_type = lhs->get_type();
6744  ASSERT_not_null(lhs_type);
6745 
6746  // DQ (4/15/2013): This is required for test2005_129.C
6747  SgType* stripped_lhs_type = lhs_type->stripType (SgType::STRIP_MODIFIER_TYPE|SgType::STRIP_ARRAY_TYPE|SgType::STRIP_TYPEDEF_TYPE);
6748  ASSERT_not_null(stripped_lhs_type);
6749 
6750  SgPointerType* pointerType = isSgPointerType (stripped_lhs_type);
6751 
6752  if ( (pointerType == NULL) && (isSgArrowExp(binary_op) == NULL) )
6753  {
6754  if (parent_function_call_uses_operator_syntax == true)
6755  {
6756  // This addresses the requirement of test2013_97.C
6757  returnValue = false;
6758  }
6759  else
6760  {
6761  returnValue = true;
6762  }
6763  }
6764  else
6765  {
6766  if (pointerType != NULL && isSgArrowExp(binary_op) != NULL)
6767  {
6768  SgFunctionCallExp* functionCallExp = isSgFunctionCallExp(lhs);
6769  ASSERT_not_null(functionCallExp);
6770 
6771  SgDotExp* dotExp = isSgDotExp(functionCallExp->get_function());
6772  ASSERT_not_null(dotExp);
6773 
6774  SgMemberFunctionRefExp* memberFunctionRefExp = isSgMemberFunctionRefExp(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6775  if (memberFunctionRefExp != nullptr)
6776  {
6777  SgMemberFunctionDeclaration* memberFunctionDeclaration = memberFunctionRefExp->getAssociatedMemberFunctionDeclaration();
6778  ASSERT_not_null(memberFunctionDeclaration);
6779  if (memberFunctionDeclaration->get_name() == "operator->")
6780  {
6781  // Avoid putting out "->->"
6782  returnValue = false;
6783  }
6784  else
6785  {
6786  returnValue = true;
6787  }
6788  }
6789  else
6790  {
6791  returnValue = true;
6792  }
6793  }
6794  else
6795  {
6796  // This is the case for test2013_121.C
6797  returnValue = true;
6798  }
6799  }
6800 
6801  return returnValue;
6802  }

6805 void
6806 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseValue(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
6807  {
6808  SgValueExp* valueExp = isSgValueExp(expr);
6809  ASSERT_not_null(valueExp);
6810 
6811  SgExpression* expressionTree = valueExp->get_originalExpressionTree();
6812  if (expressionTree != NULL && info.SkipConstantFoldedExpressions() == false)
6813  {
6814  switch (valueExp->variantT())
6815  {
6816  // Handle enums so that they will be unparsed as "enum name" instead of as integers
6817  // bool does not require special handling.
6818  case V_SgEnumVal: { unparseEnumVal(expr, info); break; }
6819  default:
6820  {
6821  unparseExpression(expressionTree,info);
6822  }
6823  }
6824  }
6825  else
6826  {
6827  switch (valueExp->variantT())
6828  {
6829  case V_SgBoolValExp: { unparseBoolVal(expr, info); break; }
6830  case V_SgCharVal: { unparseCharVal(expr, info); break; }
6831  case V_SgShortVal: { unparseShortVal(expr, info); break; }
6832  case V_SgSignedCharVal: { unparseSCharVal(expr, info); break; }
6833  case V_SgUnsignedCharVal: { unparseUCharVal(expr, info); break; }
6834  case V_SgWcharVal: { unparseWCharVal(expr, info); break; }
6835  case V_SgChar16Val: { unparseChar16Val(expr, info); break; }
6836  case V_SgChar32Val: { unparseChar32Val(expr, info); break; }
6837  case V_SgStringVal: { unparseStringVal(expr, info); break; }
6838  case V_SgUnsignedShortVal: { unparseUShortVal(expr, info); break; }
6839  case V_SgEnumVal: { unparseEnumVal(expr, info); break; }
6840  case V_SgIntVal: { unparseIntVal(expr, info); break; }
6841  case V_SgUnsignedIntVal: { unparseUIntVal(expr, info); break; }
6842  case V_SgLongIntVal: { unparseLongIntVal(expr, info); break; }
6843  case V_SgLongLongIntVal: { unparseLongLongIntVal(expr, info); break; }
6844  case V_SgUnsignedLongLongIntVal: { unparseULongLongIntVal(expr, info); break; }
6845  case V_SgUnsignedLongVal: { unparseULongIntVal(expr, info); break; }
6846  case V_SgFloatVal: { unparseFloatVal(expr, info); break; }
6847  case V_SgDoubleVal: { unparseDoubleVal(expr, info); break; }
6848  case V_SgLongDoubleVal: { unparseLongDoubleVal(expr, info); break; }
6849  case V_SgComplexVal: { unparseComplexVal(expr, info); break; }
6850  case V_SgNullptrValExp: { unparseNullptrVal(expr, info); break; }
6851 
6852  default:
6853  {
6854  printf ("Default reached in switch statement valueExp = %p = %s \n",valueExp,valueExp->class_name().c_str());
6855  ROSE_ABORT();
6856  }
6857 
6858  }
6859  }
6860  }

6881

6894  {

6897  }
6898 
6899  if (unp->opt.get_num_opt() || (C_language_support == true))
6900  {
6901  // The C language does not support boolean values (C99 does, as I recall)
6902  // we want to print the boolean values as numerical values
6903  // DQ (11/29/2009): get_value() returns an "int" and MSVC issues a warning for mixed type predicates.
6904  // if (bool_val->get_value() == true)
6905  if (bool_val->get_value() != 0)
6906  {
6907  curprint("1");
6908  }
6909  else
6910  {
6911  curprint("0");
6912  }
6913  }
6914  else
6915  {
6916  // This is the C++ case (and any language supporting boolean values).
6917 
6918  // print them as "true" or "false"
6919  // DQ (11/29/2009): get_value() returns an "int" and MSVC issues a warning for mixed type predicates.
6920  if (bool_val->get_value() != 0)
6921  {
6922  curprint("true");
6923  }
6924  else
6925  {
6926  curprint("false");
6927  }

6947 void
6948 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseCharVal(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info &)
6949  {
6950  SgCharVal* char_val = isSgCharVal(expr);
6951  ASSERT_not_null(char_val);
6952 
6953  // DQ (9/30/2006): Use the string where it is available (I think the string
6954  // based literals for non-floating point cases are not finished yet).
6955  if (char_val->get_valueString() == "")
6956  {
6957  // curprint ( char_val->get_value();
6958 
6959  // DQ (3/19/2005): Many different literal characters were not being output properly or were being output as
6960  // integers which when used as function parameters lead to the wrong function resolution.
6961  // We can't just output the integer conversion of the character since where this is used as a function
6962  // argument it will match a different function prototype (which might not even exist) (see bug 2005_30.C).
6963  // curprint ( (int) char_val->get_value();
6964  switch(char_val->get_value())
6965  {
6966  case '\0': curprint ( "\'\\0\'"); break;
6967  case '\1': curprint ( "\'\\1\'"); break;
6968  case '\2': curprint ( "\'\\2\'"); break;
6969  case '\3': curprint ( "\'\\3\'"); break;
6970  case '\4': curprint ( "\'\\4\'"); break;
6971  case '\5': curprint ( "\'\\5\'"); break;
6972  case '\6': curprint ( "\'\\6\'"); break;
6973  // EDG complains that \7, \8, and \9 are redundent (and EDG is correct!)
6974  // This case is replicated with ASCII BS case '\a' (below)
6975  // case '\7': curprint ( "\'\\7\'"; break;
6976  // This case is replicated with ASCI BEL case '\b' (below)
6977  // case '\8': curprint ( "\'\\8\'"; break;
6978  // This case is replicated with ASCI HT case '\t' (below)
6979  // case '\9': curprint ( "\'\\9\'"; break;
6980  // Note that if we skip this case then '\b' is converted to '^H' which is likely
6981  // equivalant but is different enough to be annoying. Likely other literals have
6982  // similar equivalants. I now expect that '^H' is the wrong translation of '\b'.
6983  // So the cases below are required.
6984  case '\n': curprint ( "\'\\n\'"); break;
6985  case '\t': curprint ( "\'\\t\'"); break;
6986  case '\v': curprint ( "\'\\v\'"); break;
6987  case '\b': curprint ( "\'\\b\'"); break;
6988  case '\r': curprint ( "\'\\r\'"); break;
6989  case '\f': curprint ( "\'\\f\'"); break;
6990  case '\a': curprint ( "\'\\a\'"); break;
6991  case '\'': curprint ( "\'\\'\'"); break;
6992  case '\"': curprint ( "\'\"\'"); break;
6993  // Handle special case of ASCI DEL (decimal 127)
6994  // case '\177': curprint ( "\'\177\'"; break;
6995  // case 127: curprint ( "\'\177\'"; break;
6996  case 127: curprint ( "char(127)"); break;
6997  // This case is required since "\\" is the C++ name of the ASCII "\" character
6998  case '\\': curprint ( "\'\\\\'"); break;
6999 
7000 #if 0
7001  // DQ (3/19/2005): These should no longer be required, since they are handled properly by the C++ string output!
7002  // Provide these cases explicitly so that '0' is not converted to '48'
7003  // (which is a multi-character character constant, not what we want!)
7004  case '0': curprint ( "\'0\'"); break;
7005  case '1': curprint ( "\'1\'"); break;
7006  case '2': curprint ( "\'2\'"); break;
7007  case '3': curprint ( "\'3\'"); break;
7008  case '4': curprint ( "\'4\'"); break;
7009  case '5': curprint ( "\'5\'"); break;
7010  case '6': curprint ( "\'6\'"); break;
7011  case '7': curprint ( "\'7\'"); break;
7012  case '8': curprint ( "\'8\'"); break;
7013  case '9': curprint ( "\'9\'"); break;
7014 
7015  case '\?': curprint ( "\'\\?\'"); break;
7016  case '`': curprint ( "\'`\'"); break;
7017  case '~': curprint ( "\'~\'"); break;
7018  case '_': curprint ( "\'_\'"); break;
7019 #endif
7020  default:
7021  {
7022  // I could not get char to be output as anything but an integer, so I converted the char to a string
7023  // and then output the string this resulted in not every case (value of char) requiring special handling.
7024  // Generate a C string and copy it to a C++ string and then output the C++ string so that we
7025  // can leverage the C++ string handling of character literals.
7026  char c[2];
7027  c[0] = char_val->get_value();
7028  c[1] = '\0';
7029  string s = c;
7030  // curprint ( "\'" + (char)char_val->get_value() + "\'";
7031  curprint ( "\'" + s + "\'");
7032  break;
7033  }
7034  }
7035  }
7036  else
7037  {
7038  // Use the string representing the literal where it is available
7039  curprint ( char_val->get_valueString());
7040  }
7041  }

7199  // DQ (5/29/2011): Newest refactored support for name qualification.

7201  SgName nameQualifier = enum_val->get_qualified_name_prefix();

7205  // of qualification triggers possible (likely) over qualification. Overqualification is generally the default
7206  // this flag is sometime taken to mean that the "::" is required as well.

7211  if (enum_val->get_requiresNameQualification() == true)

7216  }
7217 
7218  // DQ (6/9/2011): Newest refactored support for name qualification.
7219  // SgName nameQualifier = unp->u_name->generateNameQualifier(enum_val->get_declaration(),info);
7220  SgName nameQualifier = enum_val->get_qualified_name_prefix();
7221 #if DEBUG_UNPARSE_ENUM_VAL
7222  printf ("In Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseEnumVal: nameQualifier = %s \n",nameQualifier.str());
7223 #endif
7224  // DQ (8/31/2012): If we are going to NOT output a name, then we had better not out any name qualification.
7225  if (enum_val->get_name().is_null() == true)
7226  {
7227  printf ("If the enum name does not exist, then we can't qualify it nameQualifier = %s (reset) \n",(nameQualifier.is_null() == false) ? nameQualifier.str() : "NULL");
7228  nameQualifier = "";
7229  ROSE_ASSERT(nameQualifier.is_null() == true);
7230  }
7231 #endif
7232 #if DEBUG_UNPARSE_ENUM_VAL
7233  printf ("enum value's nameQualifier = %s \n",(nameQualifier.is_null() == false) ? nameQualifier.str() : "NULL");
7234 #endif
7235  if (nameQualifier.is_null() == false)
7236  {
7237  curprint ( nameQualifier.str() );
7238  }
7239  }
7240  }
7241  else
7242  {
7243  ROSE_ASSERT (enum_val->get_name().is_null() == false);
7244  printf ("Warning in Unparser::unparseEnumVal(): no associated enum declaration specificed for enum value = %s \n",enum_val->get_name().str());
7245  }
7246 
7247 #if DEBUG_UNPARSE_ENUM_VAL
7248  printf ("In Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseEnumVal: enum_val->get_name().is_null() = %s \n",enum_val->get_name().is_null() ? "true" : "false");
7249 #endif
7250  // DQ (8/31/2012): We need to allow for values that would not be mapped to enum names and in this case
7251  // are output as enum values (see test2012_202.C for an example of this).
7252 
7253  // DQ (11/4/2012): Detect if this is a generated name with an cast from an un-named type (we can't output these names).
7254  SgName enum_value_name = enum_val->get_name();
7255  SgName substring = enum_value_name.head(strlen("__anonymous_"));
7256  bool isGeneratedName = (substring == "__anonymous_");
7257 #if DEBUG_UNPARSE_ENUM_VAL
7258  printf ("enum_value_name = %s \n",enum_value_name.str());
7259  printf ("substring = %s \n",substring.str());
7260  printf ("isGeneratedName = %s \n",isGeneratedName ? "true" : "false");
7261 #endif
7262 
7263  // DQ (11/4/2012): Never output a generated name since it will cause link failures
7264  // (and frequently also interpretation as implicit function calls in C).
7265  // if (enum_val->get_name().is_null() == false)
7266  if ( (enum_val->get_name().is_null() == false) && (isGeneratedName == false) )
7267  {
7268  // This is the typical case.
7269  // curprint(enum_val->get_name().str());
7270 
7271  // DQ (5/14/2018): For C++11 enum class declarations, the assocated enum value will
7272  // ALWAYS require an explicit cast or additional name qualification.
7273  SgEnumDeclaration* enumDeclaration = enum_val->get_declaration();
7274  if (enumDeclaration != NULL)
7275  {
7276  if (enumDeclaration->get_isScopedEnum() == true)
7277  {
7278  // curprint(enum_val->get_name().str());
7279  curprint(enumDeclaration->get_name().str());
7280  curprint("(");
7281  string valueString = StringUtility::numberToString(enum_val->get_value());
7282  curprint(valueString);
7283  curprint(")");
7284  }
7285  else
7286  {
7287  curprint(enum_val->get_name().str());
7288  }
7289  }
7290  else
7291  {
7292  curprint(enum_val->get_name().str());
7293  }
7294  }
7295  else
7296  {
7297  curprint(tostring(enum_val->get_value()));
7298  }
7299  }
7300  }

7400 void
7401 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseFloatVal(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info &)
7402  {
7403  SgFloatVal* float_val = isSgFloatVal(expr);
7404  ASSERT_not_null(float_val);
7405 
7406 
7407  // DQ (10/18/2005): Need to handle C code which cannot use C++ mechanism to specify
7408  // infinity, quiet NaN, and signaling NaN values. Note that we can't use the C++
7409  // interface since the input program, and thus the generated code, might not have
7410  // included the "limits" header file.
7411  float float_value = float_val->get_value();
7412 
7413  if (float_value == std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity())
7414  {
7415  // Because of Fortran kind (compiler dependent) the string literal may be a double.
7416  // Thus it makes more sense to print the original string literal [Rasmussen 4/28/2019].
7417  if (SageInterface::is_Fortran_language() && float_val->get_valueString().length() > 0)
7418  {
7419  curprint(float_val->get_valueString());
7420  }
7421  else
7422  {
7423  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity()";
7424  curprint( "__builtin_huge_valf()");
7425  }
7426  }
7427  else
7428  {
7429  // Test for NaN value (famous test of to check for equality) or check for C++ definition of NaN.
7430  // We detect C99 and C "__NAN__" in EDG, but translate to backend specific builtin function.
7431  if ((float_value != float_value) || (float_value == std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN()) )
7432  {
7433  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN()";
7434  curprint( "__builtin_nanf (\"\")");
7435  }
7436  else
7437  {
7438  if (float_value == std::numeric_limits<float>::signaling_NaN())
7439  {
7440  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<float>::signaling_NaN()";
7441  curprint("__builtin_nansf (\"\")");
7442  }
7443  else
7444  {
7445  // typical case!
7446  // curprint ( float_val->get_value();
7447  // AS (11/08/2005) add support for values as string
7448  if (float_val->get_valueString() == "")
7449  {
7450  curprint(tostring(float_val->get_value()));
7451  }
7452  else
7453  {
7454  curprint(float_val->get_valueString());
7455  }
7456  }
7457  }
7458  }
7459  }

7656 #define DEBUG__unparseExprList 0
7657 
7658 void UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseExprList(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
7659  {
7660  SgExprListExp* expr_list = isSgExprListExp(expr);
7661  ASSERT_not_null(expr_list);
7662 
7663 #if DEBUG__unparseExprList
7664  printf ("Enter unparseExprList():\n");
7665  printf (" expr = %p = %s\n", expr, expr->class_name().c_str());
7666  printf (" ->get_type() = %p = %s\n", expr->get_type(), expr->get_type()->class_name().c_str());
7667 #endif
7668 
7669  SgExpressionPtrList::iterator i = expr_list->get_expressions().begin();
7670 
7671  if (i != expr_list->get_expressions().end())
7672  {
7673  while (i != expr_list->get_expressions().end())
7674  {
7675  SgExpression* argument_expr = *i;
7676  SgType * argument_type = argument_expr->get_type();
7677 #if DEBUG__unparseExprList
7678  printf (" - argument_expr = %p = %s \n", argument_expr, argument_expr->class_name().c_str());
7679  printf (" argument_type = %p = %s \n", argument_type, argument_type->class_name().c_str());
7680 #endif
7681  bool context_for_added_parentheses = info.get_context_for_added_parentheses();
7682  bool needParen = isSgFunctionType(argument_type) && !context_for_added_parentheses;
7683 #if DEBUG__unparseExprList
7684  printf (" context_for_added_parentheses = %s\n", context_for_added_parentheses ? "true" : "false");
7685  printf (" needParen = %s\n", needParen ? "true" : "false");
7686 #endif
7687  SgConstructorInitializer* ctor_init = isSgConstructorInitializer(argument_expr);
7688  if (ctor_init != NULL)
7689  {
7690  SgNode * p_expr_list = expr_list ? expr_list->get_parent() : nullptr;
7691  SgNode * pp_expr_list = p_expr_list ? p_expr_list->get_parent() : nullptr;
7692 #if DEBUG__unparseExprList
7693  printf (" p_expr_list = %p = %s \n", p_expr_list, p_expr_list->class_name().c_str());
7694  printf (" pp_expr_list = %p = %s \n", pp_expr_list, pp_expr_list->class_name().c_str());
7695 #endif
7696  SgInitializedName * ctor_init_parent_iname = isSgConstructorInitializer(p_expr_list) ? isSgInitializedName(pp_expr_list) : nullptr;
7697  bool iname_use_cpy_syntax = ctor_init_parent_iname ? ctor_init_parent_iname->get_using_assignment_copy_constructor_syntax() : false;
7698  needParen |= ctor_init_parent_iname && !iname_use_cpy_syntax;
7699 
7700  bool this_constructor_initializer_is_using_Cxx11_initializer_list = isAssociatedWithCxx11_initializationList(ctor_init);
7701 #if DEBUG__unparseExprList
7702  printf (" this_constructor_initializer_is_using_Cxx11_initializer_list = %s \n",this_constructor_initializer_is_using_Cxx11_initializer_list ? "true" : "false");
7703  printf (" ctor_init->get_is_braced_initialized() = %s \n", ctor_init->get_is_braced_initialized() ? "true" : "false");
7704 #endif
7705  if (this_constructor_initializer_is_using_Cxx11_initializer_list) needParen = false;
7706  if (ctor_init->get_is_braced_initialized()) needParen = false;
7707  }
7708 #if DEBUG__unparseExprList
7709  printf (" needParen = %s\n", needParen ? "true" : "false");
7710 #endif
7711 
7712  if (needParen) curprint("(");
7713  SgUnparse_Info newinfo(info);
7714  newinfo.set_SkipBaseType();
7715  unparseExpression(*i, newinfo);
7716  if (needParen) curprint(")");
7717 
7718  i++;
7719  if (i != expr_list->get_expressions().end()) curprint ( ",");
7720  }
7721  }
7722 
7723 #if DEBUG__unparseExprList
7724  printf ("Leaving unparseExprList()\n");
7725 #endif
7726  }

7729 void
7730 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseIncludeDirectiveStatement (SgStatement* stmt, SgUnparse_Info& info)
7731  {
7732  SgIncludeDirectiveStatement* directive = isSgIncludeDirectiveStatement(stmt);
7733  ASSERT_not_null(directive);
7734  ASSERT_not_null(info.get_current_source_file());
7735  bool usingTokenUnparsing = info.get_current_source_file()->get_unparse_tokens();
7736 
7737  printf ("In unparseIncludeDirectiveStatement: usingTokenUnparsing = %s \n",usingTokenUnparsing ? "true" : "false");
7738 
7739  // DQ (12/1/2018): This code may be required when unparsing using the header file unparsing support but not using the token unparsing.
7740  if (usingTokenUnparsing == false)
7741  {
7742  // DQ (9/24/2018): I think we want CPP directivs to be unparsed from the SgAttachedPreprocessingInfo lists on statements, instead of seperately.
7743  // This is the better choice because then the other comments and any other CPP directives will be unparsed as in the original code.
7744  // NOTE: If we don't suppores this here, then there will be two include directives unparsed.
7745  SgHeaderFileBody* headerFileBody = directive -> get_headerFileBody();
7746  printf ("In unparseIncludeDirectiveStatement(): headerFileBody = %p \n",headerFileBody);
7747 
7748  if (headerFileBody != nullptr)
7749  {
7750  if (headerFileBody -> get_file_info() -> get_filenameString() == getFileName())
7751  {
7752  unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(headerFileBody, info, PreprocessingInfo::after); //Its always "after" if attached to a header file body.
7753  }
7754  }
7755  else
7756  {
7757  // DQ (3/24/2019): The newest use of this IR nodes does not accomidate the headerFileBody.
7758  ASSERT_not_null(directive);
7759  curprint("\n ");
7760  unp->cur.insert_newline(1);
7761 
7762  curprint(directive->get_directiveString());
7763  unp->cur.insert_newline(1);
7764  }
7765  }
7766  }

7768 void

8001  ASSERT_not_null(c);
8002  curprint(string(" default("));
8003  SgOmpClause::omp_default_option_enum dv = c->get_data_sharing();
8004  switch (dv)
8005  {
8006  case SgOmpClause::e_omp_default_none:
8007  {
8008  curprint(string("none"));
8009  break;
8010  }
8011  case SgOmpClause::e_omp_default_shared:
8012  {
8013  curprint(string("shared"));
8014  break;
8015  }
8016  case SgOmpClause::e_omp_default_private:
8017  {
8018  curprint(string("private"));
8019  break;
8020  }
8021  case SgOmpClause::e_omp_default_firstprivate:
8022  {
8023  curprint(string("firstprivate"));
8024  break;
8025  }
8026  default:
8027  cerr<<"Error: UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseOmpDefaultClause() meets unacceptable default option value:"<<dv<<endl;
8028  ROSE_ABORT ();
8029  }
8030  curprint(string(")"));
8031 }

8375 void UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseOmpVariablesClause(SgOmpClause* clause, SgUnparse_Info& info)
8376 {
8377  ASSERT_not_null(clause);
8378  SgOmpVariablesClause* c= isSgOmpVariablesClause (clause);
8379  ASSERT_not_null(c);
8380  bool is_map = false;
8381  bool is_depend= false;
8382  // unparse the clause name first
8383  switch (c->variantT())
8384  {
8385  case V_SgOmpCopyinClause:
8386  curprint(string(" copyin("));
8387  break;
8388  case V_SgOmpCopyprivateClause:
8389  curprint(string(" copyprivate("));
8390  break;
8391  case V_SgOmpFirstprivateClause:
8392  curprint(string(" firstprivate("));
8393  break;
8394  case V_SgOmpLastprivateClause:
8395  curprint(string(" lastprivate("));
8396  break;
8397  case V_SgOmpPrivateClause:
8398  curprint(string(" private("));
8399  break;
8400  case V_SgOmpUniformClause:
8401  curprint(string(" uniform("));
8402  break;
8403  case V_SgOmpAlignedClause:
8404  curprint(string(" aligned("));
8405  break;
8406  case V_SgOmpReductionClause:
8407  {
8408  curprint(string(" reduction("));
8409  //reductionOperatorToString() will handle language specific issues
8410  curprint(reductionOperatorToString(isSgOmpReductionClause(c)->get_operation()));
8411  curprint(string(" : "));
8412  break;
8413  }
8414  case V_SgOmpDependClause:
8415  {
8416  curprint(string(" depend("));
8417  curprint(dependenceTypeToString(isSgOmpDependClause(c)->get_dependence_type()));
8418  curprint(string(" : "));
8419  is_depend = true;
8420  break;
8421  }
8422  case V_SgOmpLinearClause:
8423  curprint(string(" linear("));
8424  break;
8425  case V_SgOmpMapClause:
8426  {
8427  is_map = true;
8428  curprint(string(" map("));
8429  curprint(mapOperatorToString(isSgOmpMapClause(c)->get_operation()));
8430  curprint(string(" : "));
8431  break;
8432  }
8433 
8434  case V_SgOmpSharedClause:
8435  curprint(string(" shared("));
8436  break;
8437  default:
8438  cerr<<"Error: unhandled clause type in UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseOmpVariablesClause ():"<< clause->class_name()<<endl;
8439  ROSE_ABORT();
8440  }
8441 
8442  // prepare array dimension info for map variables
8443  std::map<SgSymbol*, std::vector<std::pair<SgExpression*, SgExpression*> > > dims;
8444  std::map< SgSymbol *, std::vector< std::pair< SgOmpClause::omp_map_dist_data_enum, SgExpression * > > > dist_policies;
8445  if (is_map)
8446  {
8447  SgOmpMapClause * m_clause = isSgOmpMapClause (clause);
8448  ASSERT_not_null(m_clause);
8449  dims = m_clause->get_array_dimensions();
8450  dist_policies = m_clause->get_dist_data_policies();
8451  }
8452  else if (is_depend) // task depend(A[i:BS][j:BS]) , is also stored as array section.
8453  // TODO: long term, we need a dedicated array section AST node
8454  {
8455  SgOmpDependClause* m_clause = isSgOmpDependClause (clause);
8456  ASSERT_not_null(m_clause);
8457  dims = m_clause->get_array_dimensions();
8458  }
8459 
8460  //unparse variable list then
8461  SgExpressionPtrList::iterator p = c->get_variables()->get_expressions().begin();
8462  while ( p != c->get_variables()->get_expressions().end() )
8463  {
8464  // We now try to put array reference expression into variable list.
8465  if (SgPntrArrRefExp* aref = isSgPntrArrRefExp(*p))
8466  {
8467  // curprint (aref->unparseToString()); // This does not work!
8468  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
8469  unparseExpression(aref, ninfo);
8470  }
8471  else if (SgVarRefExp* vref= isSgVarRefExp(*p))
8472  {
8473  SgInitializedName* init_name = vref->get_symbol()->get_declaration();
8474  SgName tmp_name = init_name->get_name();
8475  curprint( tmp_name.str());
8476  SgVariableSymbol * sym = isSgVarRefExp(*p)->get_symbol();
8477  ASSERT_not_null(sym);
8478  if (is_map)
8479  {
8480  std::vector<std::pair<SgExpression*, SgExpression*> > bounds = dims[sym];
8481  if (bounds.size() >0)
8482  {
8483  std::vector<std::pair<SgExpression*, SgExpression*> >:: const_iterator iter;
8484  for (iter = bounds.begin(); iter != bounds.end(); iter ++)
8485  {
8486  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
8487  std::pair<SgExpression*, SgExpression*> bound = (*iter);
8488  SgExpression* lower = bound.first;
8489  SgExpression* upper = bound.second;
8490  ASSERT_not_null(lower);
8491  ASSERT_not_null(upper);
8492 
8493  curprint(string("["));
8494  // curprint(lower->unparseToString());
8495  unparseExpression(lower, ninfo);
8496  curprint(string(":"));
8497  // curprint(upper->unparseToString());
8498  unparseExpression(upper, ninfo);
8499  curprint(string("]"));
8500 
8501  std::vector< std::pair< SgOmpClause::omp_map_dist_data_enum, SgExpression * > > policies = dist_policies[sym];
8502  if (policies.size() !=0)
8503  unparseMapDistDataPoliciesToString (policies, ninfo);
8504  //curprint(mapDistDataPoliciesToString (policies));
8505 
8506  } // end for
8507  } // end if has bounds
8508  } // end if map
8509  else if (is_depend)
8510  {
8511  std::vector<std::pair<SgExpression*, SgExpression*> > bounds = dims[sym];
8512  if (bounds.size() >0)
8513  {
8514  std::vector<std::pair<SgExpression*, SgExpression*> >:: const_iterator iter;
8515  for (iter = bounds.begin(); iter != bounds.end(); iter ++)
8516  {
8517  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
8518  std::pair<SgExpression*, SgExpression*> bound = (*iter);
8519  SgExpression* lower = bound.first;
8520  SgExpression* upper = bound.second;
8521  ASSERT_not_null(lower);
8522  ASSERT_not_null(upper);
8523 
8524  curprint(string("["));
8525  unparseExpression(lower, ninfo);
8526  curprint(string(":"));
8527  unparseExpression(upper, ninfo);
8528  curprint(string("]"));
8529  } // end for
8530  } // end if has bounds
8531  }
8532  }
8533  else
8534  {
8535  cerr<<"Unhandled type of variable in a varlist:"<< (*p)->class_name()<<endl;
8536  ROSE_ABORT ();
8537  }
8538 
8539  // output the optional dimension info for map() variable
8540  // Move to the next argument
8541  p++;
8542 
8543  // Check if this is the last argument (output a "," separator if not)
8544  if (p != c->get_variables()->get_expressions().end())
8545  {
8546  curprint( ",");
8547  }
8548  }
8549 
8550  // optional :step for linear(list:step)
8551  if (isSgOmpLinearClause(c) && isSgOmpLinearClause(c)->get_step())
8552  {
8553  curprint(string(":"));
8554  unparseExpression(isSgOmpLinearClause(c)->get_step(), info);
8555  }
8556 
8557  // optional :alignment for aligned(list:alignment)
8558  if (isSgOmpAlignedClause(c) && isSgOmpAlignedClause(c)->get_alignment())
8559  {
8560  curprint(string(":"));
8561  unparseExpression(isSgOmpAlignedClause(c)->get_alignment(), info);
8562  }
8563 
8564  curprint(string(")"));
8565 }
8566 
8567 void UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseOmpExpressionClause(SgOmpClause* clause, SgUnparse_Info& info)
8568 {
8569  ASSERT_not_null(clause);
8570  SgOmpExpressionClause * c = isSgOmpExpressionClause (clause);
8571  ROSE_ASSERT (c);
8572  SgOmpExpressionClause* exp_clause = isSgOmpExpressionClause(c);
8573  ROSE_ASSERT(exp_clause);
8574 
8575 
8576  // ordered (n) vs ordered : (n) is optional
8577  if (isSgOmpOrderedClause(c) && (exp_clause->get_expression() == NULL))
8578  {
8579  curprint(string(" ordered"));
8580  return;
8581  }
8582 
8583  if (isSgOmpCollapseClause(c))
8584  curprint(string(" collapse("));
8585  else if (isSgOmpIfClause(c))
8586  curprint(string(" if("));
8587  else if (isSgOmpOrderedClause(c))
8588  curprint(string(" ordered("));
8589  else if (isSgOmpFinalClause(c))
8590  curprint(string(" final("));
8591  else if (isSgOmpPriorityClause(c))
8592  curprint(string(" priority("));
8593  else if (isSgOmpNumThreadsClause(c))
8594  curprint(string(" num_threads("));
8595  else if (isSgOmpDeviceClause(c))
8596  curprint(string(" device("));
8597  else if (isSgOmpSafelenClause(c))
8598  curprint(string(" safelen("));
8599  else if (isSgOmpSimdlenClause(c))
8600  curprint(string(" simdlen("));
8601  else {
8602  cerr<<"Error: unacceptable clause type within unparseOmpExpressionClause():"<< clause->class_name()<<endl;
8603  ROSE_ABORT();
8604  }
8605 
8606  // unparse the expression
8607  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
8608  if (exp_clause->get_expression())
8609  unparseExpression(exp_clause->get_expression(), ninfo);
8610  else
8611  {
8612  cerr<<"Error: missing expression within unparseOmpExpressionClause():"<< clause->class_name()<<endl;
8613  ROSE_ABORT();
8614  }
8615 
8616  curprint(string(")"));
8617 }

8619 // Entry point for unparsing OpenMP clause
8620 void UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseOmpClause(SgOmpClause* clause, SgUnparse_Info& info)
8621 {
8622  ASSERT_not_null(clause);
8623  switch (clause->variantT())
8624  {
8625  case V_SgOmpDefaultClause:
8626  {
8627  unparseOmpDefaultClause(isSgOmpDefaultClause(clause),info);
8628  break;
8629  }
8630  case V_SgOmpProcBindClause:
8631  {
8632  unparseOmpProcBindClause(isSgOmpProcBindClause(clause),info);
8633  break;
8634  }
8635  case V_SgOmpAtomicClause:
8636  {
8637  unparseOmpAtomicClause(isSgOmpAtomicClause(clause),info);
8638  break;
8639  }
8640 
8641  case V_SgOmpNowaitClause:
8642  {
8643  curprint(string(" nowait"));
8644  break;
8645  }
8646  case V_SgOmpInbranchClause:
8647  {
8648  curprint(string(" inbranch"));
8649  break;
8650  }
8651  case V_SgOmpNotinbranchClause:
8652  {
8653  curprint(string(" notinbranch"));
8654  break;
8655  }
8656 #if 0 // this becomes an expression clause since OpenMP 4.5
8657  case V_SgOmpOrderedClause:
8658  {
8659  curprint(string(" ordered"));
8660  break;
8661  }
8662 #endif
8663  case V_SgOmpUntiedClause:
8664  {
8665  curprint(string(" untied"));
8666  break;
8667  }
8668  case V_SgOmpMergeableClause:
8669  {
8670  curprint(string(" mergeable"));
8671  break;
8672  }
8673  case V_SgOmpBeginClause:
8674  {
8675  curprint(string(" begin"));
8676  break;
8677  }
8678  case V_SgOmpEndClause:
8679  {
8680  curprint(string(" end"));
8681  break;
8682  }
8683  case V_SgOmpScheduleClause:
8684  {
8685  unparseOmpScheduleClause(isSgOmpScheduleClause(clause), info);
8686  break;
8687  }
8688  case V_SgOmpDeviceClause:
8689  case V_SgOmpCollapseClause:
8690  case V_SgOmpIfClause:
8691  case V_SgOmpFinalClause:
8692  case V_SgOmpPriorityClause:
8693  case V_SgOmpNumThreadsClause:
8694  case V_SgOmpSafelenClause:
8695  case V_SgOmpSimdlenClause:
8696  case V_SgOmpOrderedClause:
8697  //case V_SgOmpExpressionClause: // there should be no instance for this clause
8698  {
8699  unparseOmpExpressionClause(isSgOmpExpressionClause(clause), info);
8700  break;
8701  }
8702  case V_SgOmpCopyprivateClause:
8703  case V_SgOmpCopyinClause:
8704  case V_SgOmpFirstprivateClause:
8705  case V_SgOmpLastprivateClause:
8706  case V_SgOmpPrivateClause:
8707  case V_SgOmpReductionClause:
8708  case V_SgOmpDependClause:
8709  case V_SgOmpMapClause:
8710  case V_SgOmpSharedClause:
8711  case V_SgOmpUniformClause:
8712  case V_SgOmpAlignedClause:
8713  case V_SgOmpLinearClause:
8714  {
8715  unparseOmpVariablesClause(isSgOmpVariablesClause(clause), info);
8716  break;
8717  }
8718  default:
8719  {
8720  cerr<<"Unhandled OpenMP clause type in UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::unparseOmpClause():"<<clause->class_name()<<endl;
8721  ROSE_ABORT();
8722  }
8723  }
8724 }

8835  unp->u_sage->curprint_newline();
8836  switch (stmt->variantT())
8837  {

8840  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8841  curprint(string ("atomic "));

8846  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8847  curprint(string ("section "));

8849  }

8852  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8853  curprint(string ("task "));
8854  break;
8855  }

8857  {
8858  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8859  curprint(string ("taskwait "));
8860  break;
8861  }
8862  case V_SgOmpFlushStatement:
8863  {
8864  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8865  curprint(string ("flush "));
8866  break;
8867  }
8868  case V_SgOmpThreadprivateStatement:
8869  {
8870  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8871  curprint(string ("threadprivate "));
8872  break;
8873  }
8874  case V_SgOmpBarrierStatement:
8875  {
8876  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8877  curprint(string ("barrier "));
8878  break;
8879  }
8880  case V_SgOmpParallelStatement:
8881  {
8882  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8883  curprint(string ("parallel "));

8885  }
8886  case V_SgOmpTargetStatement:
8887  {
8888  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8889  curprint(string ("target "));
8890  break;
8891  }
8892  case V_SgOmpTargetDataStatement:

8894  unparseOmpPrefix(info);

8901  curprint(string ("critical "));

8903  {
8904  curprint (string ("("));
8905  curprint (isSgOmpCriticalStatement(stmt)->get_name().getString());

8908  break;

8916  case V_SgOmpForSimdStatement:

8925  curprint(string ("do "));

8927  }
8928  case V_SgOmpMasterStatement:
8929  {
8930  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8931  curprint(string ("master "));
8932  break;
8933  }
8934  case V_SgOmpOrderedStatement:
8935  {
8936  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8937  curprint(string ("ordered "));
8938  break;
8939  }
8940  case V_SgOmpWorkshareStatement:
8941  {
8942  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8943  curprint(string ("workshare "));
8944  break;
8945  }
8946  case V_SgOmpSingleStatement:
8947  {
8948  unparseOmpPrefix(info);
8949  curprint(string ("single "));
8950  break;
8951  }
8952  case V_SgOmpSimdStatement:

8970  default:

9032 PrecedenceSpecifier
9033 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::getPrecedence(SgExpression* expr)
9034  {
9035  // DQ (11/24/2007): This is a redundant mechanism for computing the precedence of expressions (NO!)
9036  // DQ (4/20/2013): Actually, this is the support for operator precedence that is correctly handling
9037  // overloaded operators to be the precedence of the operators that they are overloading, so this
9038  // is an important part of the unparser infrastructure. There is also a specifictaion of
9039  // operator precedence a static data members on each expression IR node, and this function could
9040  // and likely should use the values that are set there to avoud some level of redundancy.
9041 
9042  // DQ (2/5/2015): Added note from google search for precedence of the noexcept operator.
9043  // The standard itself doesn't specify precedence levels. They are derived from the grammar.
9044  // const_cast, static_cast, dynamic_cast, reinterpret_cast, typeid, sizeof..., noexcept and
9045  // alignof are not included since they are never ambiguous.
9046 
9047 #if PRINT_DEVELOPER_WARNINGS
9048  printf ("This is a redundant mechanism for computing the precedence of expressions \n");
9049 #endif
9050 
9051 #if 0
9052  printf ("In getPrecedence(): expr = %p = %s \n",expr,expr->class_name().c_str());
9053 #endif
9054 
9055  // This call to GetOperatorVariant will map overloaded operators for syntax (e.g. operator+())

9532 UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::getAssociativity(SgExpression* expr)
9533  {
9534  // DQ (7/23/2013): This should match the table in: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operators_in_C_and_C%2B%2B#Operator_precedence
9535  // Note also that this table has the precedence in the wrong order compared to how we have listed it in ROSE.
9536 
9537  // I have added the case for SgCastExp, but noticed that there appear to be many incorrect entries for associativity for the
9538  // other operators. This function is called in the evaluation for added "()" using the operator precedence (obtained from
9539  // the function: getPrecedence()).
9540 
9541  // DQ (9/25/2013): It is an additional issue that some associativity rules are language dependent. For example, I understand
9542  // that Fortran supports A - B - C as A - (B - C) (right associative) where as C and C++ would treat it as (A - B) - C (left
9543  // associative). Currently all associativity is defined in terms of C/C++, this is something to fix for the Fortran. In
9544  // general we add parenthesis to support the explict handling wherever possible (I think). As a rule, Fortran relational
9545  // operators are not associative. The exponentiation operator associates right to left (right associative). Thus, A**B**C
9546  // is equal to A**(B**C) rather than (A**B)**C. All other FORTRAN operators are left to right associative (left associative)
9547  // (however it appears to contradict the stated rule for minus (above).
9548 
9549  // DQ (4/20/2018): Added assertion.
9550  ASSERT_not_null(expr);
9551 
9552  int variant = GetOperatorVariant(expr);
9553 
9554 #if 0
9555  printf ("In getAssociativity(): variant = %d = %s \n",variant,Cxx_GrammarTerminalNames[variant].name.c_str());
9556  curprint(string("\n/* In getAssociativity(): variant = ") + Cxx_GrammarTerminalNames[variant].name + " */ \n");
9557 #endif
9558 
9559  switch (variant)
9560  {

9632 
9633  }
